raw:
[
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Manchester < Old English Mameceaster < *Mam + ceaster; ceaster (OE) = Roman fort/city, from Latin castra",
    "reading": "A fortified settlement near a breast-shaped hill, the Roman camp of the Mam people",
    "languages": ["en", "la", "ang"],
    "source": "Oxford English Dictionary, s.v. Manchester; Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary",
    "confidence": 0.8
  },
  {
    "operation": "phonetic_split",
    "chain": "man + chester; man (OE) = human; chester < ceaster = camp; but 'man' also sounds like 'mamm' (breast) in Celtic",
    "reading": "The human camp, or the camp of the breast-shaped mound — a place of nurture and defence",
    "languages": ["en", "cy", "la"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.6
  },
  {
    "operation": "cross_language_homophone",
    "chain": "man (fr) = hand; chester sounds like 'château' (fr) = castle; thus 'hand-castle'",
    "reading": "A hand-built fortress, a castle raised by human labour, not by nature",
    "languages": ["fr", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.5
  },
  {
    "operation": "anagram",
    "chain": "Manchester → 'chaste' + 'men' + 'er' → 'chaste men err' → 'men chase' + 'ster' (steer) → 'men chase the star'",
    "reading": "Men chase the star — a guiding light, a celestial navigation hidden in the name",
    "languages": ["en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "notariqon",
    "chain": "M-A-N-C-H-E-S-T-E-R → Mater, Anima, Numen, Corpus, Homo, Ego, Spiritus, Terra, Ego, Ratio",
    "reading": "Mother, soul, divinity, body, human, self, spirit, earth, self, reason — a microcosm of being",
    "languages": ["la", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "letter_symbol",
    "chain": "M (water, feminine) + A (beginning) + N (fish, life) + C (moon) + H (breath) + E (eye) + S (serpent) + T (cross) + E (eye) + R (sun)",
    "reading": "Water begins life; the moon breathes, the serpent sees, the cross bears the sun — a cosmic glyph",
    "languages": ["en", "he", "grc"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.3
  },
  {
    "operation": "numerical",
    "chain": "M=40, A=1, N=50, C=3, H=8, E=5, S=19, T=20, E=5, R=18 (Hebrew gematria values) → sum = 169 = 13²",
    "reading": "The square of thirteen — unity and transformation, a perfect number of death and rebirth",
    "languages": ["he", "en"],
    "source": "generative",
    "confidence": 0.4
  },
  {
    "operation": "etymology",
    "chain": "Mam (Celtic) = breast; ceaster (OE) = Roman fort; thus 'breast-fort' — a hill fort shaped like a breast",
    "reading": "A fortified breast — the earth as mother, a place of refuge and nourishment",
    "languages": ["cy", "ang", "la"],
    "source": "Oxford Dictionary of English Place-Names (Mills)",
    "confidence": 0.9
  }
]
